newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strikes disrupt French air traffic and hospitals.
newsitem.headline: Strikes disrupt French air traffic and hospitals.

text.p: Airlines TAT and Air Liberte, French units of British Airways, said on Friday they would cancel three quarters of their weekend flights because of a continuing strike by cockpit crew.
The three-day-old strike halted more than 60 percent of their flights on Friday, although management said ground staff had returned to work.

Pilots and flight engineers, protesting over pay and conditions which they say will be damaged by a merger of the two airlines, indefinitely extended their strike, which had been due to end at noon (1000 GMT) on Friday.

TAT, a domestic airline, said it would ensure 12 of 60 scheduled flights on both Saturday and Sunday. Air Liberte, which flies internationally, cancelled 38 of 50 scheduled flights, including all its Saturday flights to Morocco.

Junior hospital doctors, in the fifth week of a stoppage over government plans to cut health spending, vowed to continue their protest, although another teaching hospital, in the southwest city of Toulouse, voted to return to work.
The unions said 19 out of 26 teaching hospitals were still on strike, while the government put the figure at 17 and the percentage of strikers at 19 percent.

Representatives of the strikers, protesting against state plans to fine doctors exceeding pre-set spending targets in order to plug a gaping welfare deficit, resumed talks with aides of Social Affairs Minister Jacques Barrot after both sides said some progress was made on the dispute.
The strikers have called a protest march in Paris on Sunday and a new "health blackout" day, in which they ask other doctors to join them in giving only emergency care, on Monday.
The doctors' dispute is testing the conservative government's determination to cut public deficits to qualify for the European Union's planned single currency in 1999.
In a dispute involving truckers, two unions reached agreement over early retirement and dropped out of a strike planned for May 5. But two other unions maintained their call to stop work.
